newsitem.title: UK: British millionaire gives Labour party cash boost.
newsitem.headline: British millionaire gives Labour party cash boost.

text.p: British millionaire Matthew Harding, who owns 27 percent of Chelsea Football Club, is giving the opposition Labour party one million pounds (US$1.56 million), the Financial Times said on Friday.

This is the largest personal donation made to the party, the paper said. Harding, who has never previously made a political donation, said he was giving the money after several meetings with Labour leader Tony Blair, the newspaper added.
It said the move would be a mild embarrassment for Prime Minister John Major, a passionate supporter of the soccer club.
Labour had not planned to announce the donation until closer to its annual conference at the end of September but had confirmed Harding's support on Thursday evening, the paper said.

Harding, who made his money at insurance broker Benfield, said he had "never believed that being wealthy means being Tory (Conservative)" and that Labour had a "greater understanding of enterprise" than many Conservatives, it added.
